title: Reproductive Comprehensive Set 1: Menstrual Cycle (Short Answer)

questions.prompt: Identify the two main phases of the 28-day menstrual cycle and specify which one is constant in duration and which one is variable.
questions.modelAnswer: Follicular phase (variable) and Luteal phase (constant at 14 days).

questions.prompt: What is the average duration of the follicular phase in a standard 28-day cycle, and what is its alternative name based on endometrial activity?
questions.modelAnswer: 14 days; Proliferative phase.

questions.prompt: Which hormone is primarily responsible for the proliferation of the endometrial lining, and which ovarian cells are its primary source?
questions.modelAnswer: 17β-estradiol (estrogen); Granulosa cells.

questions.prompt: Describe the specific pattern of GnRH secretion required to drive the menstrual cycle and the consequence of switching to a continuous infusion.
questions.modelAnswer: Pulsatile secretion; continuous secretion down-regulates receptors and inhibits FSH/LH secretion.

questions.prompt: By what day of the cycle is a single "dominant" follicle typically selected for ovulation?
questions.modelAnswer: Days 5-7.

questions.prompt: Explain the "positive feedback" event that occurs at mid-cycle. Which hormone triggers it, and what specific threshold must be met?
questions.modelAnswer: High levels of estradiol (at least 200 pg/mL) trigger the LH surge via positive feedback on the anterior pituitary.

questions.prompt: What are the two primary actions of the LH surge on the follicle and the oocyte?
questions.modelAnswer: Rupture of the dominant follicle (ovulation) and completion of the first meiotic division of the oocyte.

questions.prompt: Describe the characteristics of cervical mucus during the late follicular phase. What is "ferning" and what is its physiologic purpose?
questions.modelAnswer: Watery, copious, and elastic; "ferning" refers to the salt crystallization pattern that indicates channels for sperm penetration.

questions.prompt: What is the alternative name for the luteal phase, and which steroid hormone is its dominant secretory product?
questions.modelAnswer: Secretory phase; Progesterone.

questions.prompt: Identify the endocrine structure formed from the ruptured follicle after ovulation and name the pituitary hormone that maintains it during the luteal phase.
questions.modelAnswer: Corpus luteum; Luteinizing Hormone (LH).

questions.prompt: How does progesterone affect the hypothalamic thermoregulatory center, and how is this used to retrospectively identify ovulation?
questions.modelAnswer: It increases the hypothalamic set-point temperature, leading to a rise in basal body temperature.

questions.prompt: Describe the effect of progesterone on the consistency of cervical mucus and its penetrability by sperm.
questions.modelAnswer: It becomes thick, non-elastic, and less abundant, making it impenetrable to sperm.

questions.prompt: What specific vascular and glandular changes occur in the endometrium during the secretory phase to prepare for a fertilized egg?
questions.modelAnswer: Uterine glands become tortuous and accumulate glycogen; spiral arteries elongate and become coiled; stroma becomes edematous.

questions.prompt: Explain the mechanism of "menses." What hormonal event triggers the sloughing of the functional layer of the endometrium?
questions.modelAnswer: Regression of the corpus luteum leads to an abrupt decrease in estradiol and progesterone levels.

questions.prompt: During the luteal phase, which two hormones exert negative feedback on the anterior pituitary to suppress the development of a new cohort of follicles?
questions.modelAnswer: Progesterone and Estrogen.

questions.prompt: What happens to the corpus luteum if fertilization does not occur, and what is the name of the resulting scar tissue?
questions.modelAnswer: It regresses (involutes) and becomes the corpus albicans.

questions.prompt: According to the "two-cell theory," which hormone stimulates theca cells to produce androgens, and which hormone stimulates granulosa cells to convert those androgens to estradiol?
questions.modelAnswer: LH stimulates theca cells; FSH stimulates granulosa cells.

questions.prompt: Which non-steroidal hormone is produced by granulosa cells and provides negative feedback specifically to inhibit FSH secretion?
questions.modelAnswer: Inhibin.

questions.prompt: If a woman has a 35-day cycle, on approximately which day would ovulation occur?
questions.modelAnswer: Day 21 (14 days before the next menses).

questions.prompt: Describe the state of the spiral arteries just before the onset of menstrual bleeding.
questions.modelAnswer: They undergo intense vasoconstriction, leading to ischemic necrosis of the endometrium.
